section_summary.extract_value: This section reports that the Body Image Investment factor failed to meet internal consistency criteria, so analyses focused on the General Body Appreciation factor. ANOVAs found no significant ethnicity effects or ethnicity-by-gender interactions, a significant main effect of gender (women lower than men), and significant negative correlations between General Body Appreciation and BMI for both women (r = -0.30) and men (r = -0.22).
section_summary.evidence_source: "Because the Body Image Investment factor did not meet conservative criteria for acceptable internal consistency (\alpha \ge .80; Kline, 1999), all further analyses were conducted with the General Body Appreciation factor alone." "The results of the ANOVA indicated that there was no significant main effect of ethnicity..., and no significant ethnicity by gender interaction... On the other hand, there was a significant main effect of gender (women M = 3.32, SD = 0.86; men M = 3.67, SD = 0.78)... Finally, General Body Appreciation was significantly correlated with BMI among both women (r = -.30, p < .001) and men (r = -.22, p < .001)."
